outcome: Help authorised imaging teams prioritise worklists and review validated findings sooner without replacing radiologist interpretation.
overview: Imaging volumes rise faster than radiology capacity, and every study in a long worklist waits the same way regardless of urgency. This solution routes studies through validated AI models that suggest worklist priority and present findings for radiologist review — never replacing radiologist interpretation. It runs first in silent mode against local data, then in a controlled pilot, with confidence and limitations displayed, every accept-or-reject decision documented, and model drift monitored continuously. Deployment is conditional on local validation, a clinical safety case and the medical-device approvals the local health authority requires. The aim is earlier review of agreed priority cases with overall turnaround preserved.

benefits.text: Bring agreed priority cases to radiologist review sooner
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Clinical-adjacent claim conditional on local validation, silent-mode results and regulatory approval; radiologists retain full interpretation authority — not a diagnostic-accuracy claim

benefits.text: Preserve overall report turnaround while reprioritising the worklist
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Measured against pre-pilot RIS turnaround baselines; depends on staffing and case-mix stability during the pilot

benefits.text: Document every radiologist confirm/reject decision and monitor model drift from day one
benefits.source: Reference architecture monitoring design, Redington Healthcare catalogue,
benefits.limits: A design property of the workflow and monitoring stack, verified in testing

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); imaging data and inference stay in the approved region in the reference designs, in line with UAE and Saudi health-data regulations

notFor.situation: No formal validation pathway or willingness to run a silent-mode trial first
notFor.why: Live use before representative local validation is unsafe and contradicts the catalogue’s own gate — no live use below the approved validation threshold

notFor.situation: Expectation of autonomous reads or diagnostic reporting
notFor.why: The solution is worklist advisory and findings presentation only; interpretation remains with the radiologist, and no diagnostic claim is made beyond an authorised intended use

notFor.situation: Modality or protocol mix without representative local data
notFor.why: Model performance published elsewhere does not transfer automatically; unrepresentative data invalidates the safety case

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns the clinical safety case, radiologist governance and regulatory approvals · Duration: 10–16-week validation; 20–36 weeks to controlled production
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, imaging-integration engineer, ML validation engineer; customer radiology chair, clinical safety officer, PACS/RIS administrator, biomedical engineering, privacy and security approvers · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation and post-market monitoring obligations
1) Intended-use, data and regulatory discovery
2) De-identification and integration build
3) Retrospective validation with subgroup analysis
4) Prospective silent trial
5) Controlled pilot with safety governance
6) Stabilisation, benefit review and handover
deliverables: Protocol- and population-level performance meets agreed thresholds, including subgroups
Silent-trial results reviewed and accepted by clinical safety governance
Clinical safety case and required regulatory approvals in place before live influence
PACS reconciliation, downtime reversion and cybersecurity tests passed
Radiologist sign-off and operational UAT complete
